mainTopic: End of the first פרק of תענית (the verse about kings standing and ministers bowing, and רב נחמן בר יצחק's parallel teaching about light and gladness), the הדרן, and the opening of the second פרק (סדר תעניות כיצד) about the public fast-day ceremony.
overview: This amud finishes the first פרק of תענית with two teachings built on the same pattern. The verse in ישעיהו is read to mean that kings honor by standing and ministers honor by bowing. רבי זירא points out that the verse says 'ministers, AND they shall bow,' so ministers do both. רב נחמן בר יצחק adds that צדיקים are rewarded with light and ישרים with gladness, proven from one verse in תהלים. After the הדרן for פרק מאימתי, the second פרק opens with a משנה about the public fast-day ceremony. The תיבה is brought to the city square, and ashes are placed on it, on the leaders, and on everyone. The eldest then rebukes the people: God responds to changed deeds, not to sackcloth. An experienced, poor elder with children leads a 24-ברכה תפילה, made up of the daily eighteen plus six additions, and רבי יהודה swaps two of those additions. Each added ending recalls someone God answered, from אברהם to דוד and שלמה. A story then begins with the word מעשה and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Verse proving kings stand and ministers bow
steps.stepSummary: The verse from ישעיהו is completed to prove that kings honor by standing, and the second half of the verse is cited to prove that ministers honor by bowing.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: '…to him who is despised of men, to him who is abhorred of nations, to a servant of rulers: kings shall see and arise.' And ministers honor by bowing, as it is written: 'Ministers, and they shall bow.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof that began on the previous daf: kings show honor by standing, and ministers show honor by bowing. Each half of the rule gets its own part of the verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'kings shall see and arise' show that the king's response is standing up. The words 'ministers, and they shall bow' show that the minister's response is bowing. So the original claim divides the verse into two separate kinds of honor.

keyTerms.meaning: Kings
And they shall arise (stand up)
Ministers / officials
Bowing down (prostration)
As it is written

steps.confusionAlert: This amud begins in the middle of a verse. The teaching it proves ('not everyone stands and not everyone bows: kings stand, ministers bow') was stated just before, at the end of the previous daf.

phrases.english: to him who is despised of men, to him who is abhorred of nations
phrases.notes: Continuation of ישעיהו 49:7, which began on the previous daf.

phrases.english: to a servant of rulers
kings shall see and arise.
phrases.notes: This is the source for 'kings by standing.'

phrases.english: And ministers honor by bowing,
as it is written: 'Ministers, and they shall bow.'
phrases.notes: Note the extra 'and' (ו) before 'they shall bow.' The next step builds its challenge on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the verse-proof for a teaching stated on the previous daf.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that kings honor by standing and ministers honor by bowing.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 49:7: 'Kings shall see and arise; ministers, and they shall bow.'

steps.title: The extra 'and' shows ministers do both
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא (or רבי שמואל בר נחמני) rejects the split. Because the verse says 'ministers, AND they shall bow,' the ministers both stand and bow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא objects (and some say it was רבי שמואל בר נחמני): If the verse had said 'And ministers shall bow,' it would mean what you said. But now that it says 'Ministers, and they shall bow,' it means they did this and that: they both stood and bowed.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא attacks the second half of the previous teaching using the exact wording of the verse. He concludes that ministers do not only bow; they stand and also bow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'and' sits before the word 'bow' instead of before the word 'ministers.' This links the ministers to the earlier verb 'arise,' and then adds bowing on top of it. So the kings' half of the rule stays, but the claim that ministers only bow is rejected.

keyTerms.meaning: He strongly objected to it
And some say (it was said by someone else)
As you said
Now (that it is written this way)
They did this and that (both)

steps.confusionAlert: The objection does not say ministers fail to bow. It says ministers do MORE: they stand like the kings and also bow.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira strongly objects to this,
and some say it was Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥmani:
phrases.notes: Two different traditions about who made the objection.

phrases.english: Had it been written 'And ministers shall bow' —
it would be as you said,
now that it is written 'Ministers, and they shall bow' —
they did this and that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges and revises how step 1 reads the second half of the verse.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that ministers honor only by bowing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The placement of the 'and' joins 'ministers' to 'arise' and adds 'bow' on top of it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the ministers half of the split. The kings-by-standing half remains.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The earlier reading ignored where the conjunction ו is placed in the verse.

steps.title: Righteous get light, upright get gladness
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק offers a parallel teaching: not everyone receives light and not everyone receives gladness. צדיקים receive light; ישרים receive gladness.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: I too say something similar. Not everyone is fit for light, and not everyone is fit for gladness. The righteous are fit for light, and the upright are fit for gladness.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא presents his own teaching built on the same 'not all X' pattern as the previous teaching. Here the subject is reward instead of showing honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as kings and ministers had different ways of honoring, רב נחמן בר יצחק says different kinds of good people receive different rewards. צדיקים are matched with light, and ישרים are matched with gladness. The proofs come in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: I too say (a similar idea)
Light
Gladness / joy
The righteous
The upright

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said,
I too say:
phrases.notes: He is modeling his teaching on the previous 'not all' pattern.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הַכֹּל לְאוֹרָה, וְלֹא הַכֹּל לְשִׂמְחָה.
phrases.english: Not all are fit for light, and not all are fit for gladness.
The righteous — for light,
and the upright — for gladness.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, אַף אֲנִי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel teaching modeled on the structure of step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: צדיקים are rewarded with light; ישרים are rewarded with gladness.

steps.title: One verse proves both rewards
steps.stepSummary: Both halves of רב נחמן בר יצחק's teaching are proven from one verse in תהלים: 'Light is sown for the righteous, and gladness for the upright in heart.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The righteous get light, as it is written: 'Light is sown for the righteous.' And the upright get gladness, as it is written: 'And gladness for the upright in heart.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for each half of the teaching in step 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תהלים 97:11 pairs light with the צדיק and gladness with the ישרי לב. The verse separates the two groups, and each is matched with its own reward. That matching is exactly the division רב נחמן בר יצחק described.

keyTerms.meaning: Light is sown (planted, stored up)
The upright in heart

steps.whatToRemember: The first פרק ends with two 'not all' teachings. Kings stand while ministers bow (and, per רבי זירא, stand as well). צדיקים receive light while ישרים receive gladness.

phrases.english: The righteous are for light,
as it is written: 'Light is sown for the righteous.'
and for the upright, gladness,
as it is written: 'And gladness for the upright in heart.'

steps.raayaObject: רב נחמן בר יצחק's teaching that צדיקים receive light and ישרים receive gladness.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing פרק מאימתי
steps.stepSummary: The first פרק of מסכת תענית, called מאימתי, formally ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, 'From when…' (פרק מאימתי).
steps.whatsHappening: This is the traditional closing line marking the end of the first פרק. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'הדרן עלך' expresses a commitment to come back and learn this פרק again. A new פרק with a new topic starts right after it.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (the formula for finishing a פרק)
'From when' — the name of the first פרק of תענית

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'Mei'eimatai'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק that the preceding steps ended.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: End of the first פרק of תענית.

steps.title: The fast-day ceremony: ark and ashes
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה of the second פרק describes the public fast-day ceremony. The תיבה is brought to the city square, and ashes are placed on it, on the heads of the נשיא and the אב בית דין, and on everyone's head.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the order of the fast days? They take the ark out to the city square. They put burnt ashes on the ark, on the head of the נשיא, and on the head of the אב בית דין, and each and every person puts ashes on his own head.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק begins with a משנה that describes, step by step, the public ceremony held on fast days for rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ark is normally kept inside, so bringing it out to the open street is a public act of humiliation and mourning. Ashes are placed in order of rank: first on the ark, then on the two top leaders, then on everyone. Every person puts the ashes on his own head.

keyTerms.meaning: The order (procedure) of the fast days
The ark holding the ספר תורה
The city square / open street
Burnt ashes
The head of the סנהדרין
The deputy head of the court

steps.confusionAlert: The leaders have ashes placed on their heads by others, but every other person places ashes on his own head ('נותן בראשו').
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה opens the second פרק and sets the topic for the whole פרק: the ceremony and prayers of the public fast days.

phrases.english: What is the order of the fast days?
phrases.notes: Opening words and title of the second פרק.

phrases.english: They take out the ark,
to the city square,
and they place burnt ashes
on top of the ark,
and on the head of the Nasi,
and on the head of the Av Beit Din,
and each and every person places ashes on his own head.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק after the הדרן; it does not depend on the earlier discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On public fast days, the תיבה is brought to the city square, and ashes are placed on it, on the heads of the נשיא and the אב בית דין, and by each person on his own head.

steps.title: The elder's words of rebuke: real repentance matters, not outward signs
steps.stepSummary: The eldest among them tells the people that God responds to a change in actions, not to sackcloth and fasting. He proves this from the story of נינוה and from a verse in the Prophets.
steps.simpleTranslation: The eldest among them speaks words of rebuke to them: 'Our brothers! The verse about the people of נינוה does not say "God saw their sackcloth and their fasting." It says "God saw their deeds, that they turned from their evil way." And the Prophets say: "Tear your hearts, and not your clothes."'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues the fast-day ceremony. After the ashes are placed, the eldest person gives the crowd a short speech of rebuke.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ashes and the fasting are only outward signs. The elder warns that these signs alone achieve nothing. He uses two sources: in the story of נינוה, God responded to their changed deeds. In the Prophets, God asks for torn hearts, not torn garments.

keyTerms.meaning: Words of rebuke that 'conquer' and humble the heart
The people of נינוה (from ספר יונה), who did תשובה
Their sackcloth and their fasting, the outward signs of mourning
Their deeds, meaning the actual change in behavior
The books of the Prophets and Writings (here, ספר יואל)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the tone for the whole fast-day ceremony. Every outward ritual is meant to lead to real inner תשובה.

phrases.english: The eldest among them says before them
words of rebuke: 'Our brothers!'
It is not said about the people of Nineveh
'And God saw their sackcloth and their fasting,'
rather: 'And God saw their deeds,
that they turned from their evil way.'
And in the Prophets it says:
'Tear your hearts and not your garments.'

steps.triggerLanguage: הַזָּקֵן שֶׁבָּהֶן אוֹמֵר לִפְנֵיהֶן דִּבְרֵי כִבּוּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ceremony from Step 6. After the ashes, a speech of rebuke follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On a public fast, the eldest gives words of rebuke stressing that God answers real תשובה, not outward signs.

steps.title: Who is chosen to lead the prayers on a fast day
steps.stepSummary: The prayer leader must be an elder, experienced, with children to support, and poor, so that he prays with his whole heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they stand up to pray, they send down to the תיבה an elder who is experienced in leading prayer. He must have children and an empty house, so that his heart will be fully in the prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from the speech to the prayer itself. It lists what kind of person should lead the prayers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each requirement is meant to make the prayer heartfelt. A man with children to feed and nothing at home feels the community's need himself. Because of that, he will pray with full intensity.

keyTerms.meaning: They send down before the ark, meaning they appoint someone as שליח ציבור
Experienced and fluent in leading prayer
His house is empty, meaning he is poor
His heart is whole, meaning fully focused

steps.confusionAlert: 'Empty house' does not mean he lives alone. It means his house is empty of food and money, so he is poor. That is why he truly feels the drought.

phrases.english: They stood for prayer:
they send down before the ark
an elder, experienced, who has children,
and whose house is empty,
so that his heart will be whole in prayer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the speech of rebuke to the prayer service that follows.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fast-day שליח ציבור should be an elder, experienced, with children, and poor, so he prays wholeheartedly.

steps.title: Twenty-four blessings: the usual eighteen plus six more
steps.stepSummary: The prayer leader says the everyday eighteen ברכות and adds six: זכרונות, שופרות, and four chapters of תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: He says twenty-four ברכות before them: the eighteen of every day, plus six more. These are: זכרונות and שופרות; 'To God in my distress I called, and He answered me'; 'I lift my eyes to the mountains'; 'From the depths I called You, God'; and 'A prayer of the poor man when he faints.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now explains what the leader actually says. It is a longer שמונה עשרה with six extra sections for a time of crisis.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The base is the regular weekday תפילה. The six additions bring in the themes of ראש השנה (זכרונות and שופרות) along with four chapters of תהלים about crying out to God in distress. The total comes to 24.

keyTerms.meaning: Twenty-four blessings, the fast-day form of the עמידה
The eighteen blessings of the daily עמידה
Remembrances, verses about God remembering (from ראש השנה מוסף)
Verses about the שופר (from ראש השנה מוסף)

steps.confusionAlert: Today the weekday עמידה has nineteen ברכות. The משנה counts eighteen because it uses the original count, before ולמלשינים was added.

phrases.english: And he says before them twenty-four blessings:
the eighteen of every day,
and he adds to them another six,
and these are they: Remembrances and Shofarot,
'To God in my distress I called and He answered me,'
'I lift my eyes to the mountains, etc.,'
'From the depths I called You, God,'
'A prayer of the poor man when he faints.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After naming who leads the prayer, the משנה describes what he says.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On a public fast the leader says 24 ברכות: the daily 18 plus זכרונות, שופרות, and four chapters of תהלים.

steps.title: רבי יהודה replaces Remembrances and Shofarot with verses about famine and drought
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds that זכרונות and שופרות are not said. In their place come the passage about famine and plague and the passage about droughts in ירמיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: He did not need to say זכרונות and שופרות. Instead he says 'If there is famine in the land, if there is plague' and 'The word of God that came to ירמיהו about the droughts.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה disagrees with the first opinion in the משנה about two of the six extra ברכות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree there are six additions. They argue only about two of them. רבי יהודה prefers sections that speak directly about famine and drought, the actual crisis of the fast. The זכרונות and שופרות belong to ראש השנה.

keyTerms.meaning: In their place, as a replacement
Famine (from שלמה's prayer, מלכים א ח:לז)
Plague
Droughts (ירמיהו יד:א)

steps.whatToRemember: The fast-day leader adds six ברכות to the daily eighteen. The תנא קמא includes זכרונות and שופרות. רבי יהודה swaps those two for passages about famine and drought.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיָה צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר זִכְרוֹנוֹת וְשׁוֹפָרוֹת,
phrases.english: He did not need to say Remembrances and Shofarot,
rather he says in their place

phrases.aramaic: ״רָעָב כִּי יִהְיֶה בָאָרֶץ דֶּבֶר כִּי יִהְיֶה״,
phrases.english: 'If there is famine in the land, if there is plague,'

phrases.aramaic: ״אֲשֶׁר הָיָה דְבַר ה׳ אֶל יִרְמְיָהוּ עַל דִּבְרֵי הַבַּצָּרוֹת״.
phrases.english: 'That which was the word of God to Jeremiah concerning the droughts.'

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: לֹא הָיָה צָרִיךְ לוֹמַר זִכְרוֹנוֹת וְשׁוֹפָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes part of the list of six additions given in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, זכרונות and שופרות are replaced by the famine and plague passage and the drought passage.

steps.title: The ending of the first blessing: He Who answered אברהם
steps.stepSummary: The משנה begins listing the endings. The first ending recalls אברהם at הר המוריה and closes with גואל ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he says their endings. For the first, he says: 'He Who answered אברהם on הר המוריה will answer you and hear the sound of your cry on this day. Blessed are You, ה׳, Who redeems ישראל.'
steps.whatsHappening: Step 9 said the prayer leader adds special ברכות. Now the משנה tells us exactly how each of them ends, starting with the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This 'first' ending is not one of the six new ברכות. It is the regular weekday ברכה of גואל ישראל, made longer on a fast day. That is why the count reaches 'seventh' even though only six ברכות were added. אברהם at the עקדה is the first great example of God answering someone in a moment of danger.

keyTerms.meaning: Their endings: the closing lines of each ברכה
The mountain of the עקדה, where אברהם was answered
Your cry
Who redeems ישראל: the regular weekday ברכה, made longer on a fast day

steps.confusionAlert: Do not count this 'first' ending as one of the six added ברכות. It is the longer form of the everyday ברכה of גואל ישראל. That is why the list goes up to 'seventh'.

phrases.english: And he says their endings.
For the first, he says:
'He Who answered Avraham on Mount Moriah
He will answer you
and hear the sound of your cry on this day.
Blessed are You, ה׳, Who redeems Israel.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list from steps 9 and 10 by giving the exact closing words of each ברכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first fast-day ending recalls אברהם at הר המוריה and closes with גואל ישראל.

steps.title: The ending of the second blessing: He Who answered our fathers at the sea
steps.stepSummary: The second ending recalls קריעת ים סוף and closes with 'Who remembers forgotten things.' This fits זכרונות.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the second, he says: 'He Who answered our fathers at ים סוף will answer you and hear the sound of your cry on this day. Blessed are You, ה׳, Who remembers forgotten things.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the ending of the second ברכה, which is the זכרונות ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The closing 'זוכר הנשכחות' matches the theme of זכרונות, which is God remembering. At the sea, God remembered His promise to the אבות and saved their children.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sea of Reeds, which split for the Jews
Who remembers forgotten things: the closing of זכרונות
Our fathers: the generation that left מצרים

phrases.english: For the second, he says:

phrases.aramaic: ״מִי שֶׁעָנָה אֶת אֲבוֹתֵינוּ עַל יַם סוּף
phrases.english: 'He Who answered our fathers at the Red Sea
He will answer you
and hear the sound of your cry on this day.
Blessed are You, ה׳, Who remembers forgotten things.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The זכרונות ending recalls ים סוף and closes with זוכר הנשכחות.

steps.title: The ending of the third blessing: He Who answered יהושע at גלגל
steps.stepSummary: The third ending recalls יהושע at גלגל and closes with 'Who hears the תרועה.' This fits שופרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the third, he says: 'He Who answered יהושע at גלגל will answer you and hear the sound of your cry on this day. Blessed are You, ה׳, Who hears the תרועה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the ending of the third ברכה, which is the שופרות ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהושע's camp was at גלגל when they blew שופרות around יריחו and the walls fell. So the closing 'שומע תרועה' fits the שופר theme perfectly.

keyTerms.meaning: יהושע's camp near יריחו
Who hears the שופר blast: the closing of שופרות
The ברכה built around verses about the שופר

phrases.english: For the third, he says:
'He Who answered Joshua at Gilgal
He will answer you
and hear the sound of your cry on this day.
Blessed are You, ה׳, Who hears the terua.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שופרות ending recalls יהושע at גלגל and closes with שומע תרועה.

steps.title: The ending of the fourth blessing: He Who answered שמואל at מצפה
steps.stepSummary: The fourth ending recalls שמואל at מצפה and closes with 'Who hears cries.'
steps.simpleTranslation: For the fourth, he says: 'He Who answered שמואל at מצפה will answer you and hear the sound of your cry on this day. Blessed are You, ה׳, Who hears cries.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the ending of the fourth ברכה, the first of the four תהלים chapters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At מצפה, שמואל cried out to God for the people, and God answered with victory over the פלשתים. That is why this ending closes with 'שומע צעקה'. It matches the chapter 'אל ה' בצרתה לי קראתי.'

keyTerms.meaning: The place where שמואל gathered the people to pray
Who hears cries

phrases.english: For the fourth, he says:
'He Who answered Samuel at Mizpah
He will answer you
and hear the sound of your cry on this day.
Blessed are You, ה׳, Who hears cries.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fourth ending recalls שמואל at מצפה and closes with שומע צעקה.

steps.title: The ending of the fifth blessing: He Who answered אליהו on הר הכרמל
steps.stepSummary: The fifth ending recalls אליהו on הר הכרמל and closes with 'Who hears prayer.'
steps.simpleTranslation: For the fifth, he says: 'He Who answered אליהו on הר הכרמל will answer you and hear the sound of your cry on this day. Blessed are You, ה׳, Who hears prayer.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the ending of the fifth ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On הר הכרמל, אליהו prayed and fire came down from heaven, and then rain came after a long drought. That makes it a fitting example for a fast day about rain, so it closes with 'שומע תפלה'.

keyTerms.meaning: Mount Carmel, where אליהו faced the prophets of בעל
Who hears prayer

phrases.english: For the fifth, he says:
'He Who answered Elijah on Mount Carmel
He will answer you
and hear the sound of your cry on this day.
Blessed are You, ה׳, Who hears prayer.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The fifth ending recalls אליהו on הר הכרמל and closes with שומע תפלה.

steps.title: The ending of the sixth blessing: He Who answered יונה from the fish
steps.stepSummary: The sixth ending recalls יונה inside the fish and closes with 'Who answers in a time of trouble.'
steps.simpleTranslation: For the sixth, he says: 'He Who answered יונה from inside the fish will answer you and hear the sound of your cry on this day. Blessed are You, ה׳, Who answers in a time of trouble.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the ending of the sixth ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יונה prayed from the depths of the fish's belly and was answered. This matches the chapter 'ממעמקים קראתיך', 'from the depths I called You.' The closing 'העונה בעת צרה' stresses that God answers even in the worst moment.

keyTerms.meaning: The belly of the fish
Who answers in a time of trouble

phrases.english: For the sixth, he says:
'He Who answered Jonah from within the belly of the fish
He will answer you
and hear the sound of your cry on this day.

phrases.aramaic: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה ה׳ הָעוֹנֶה בְּעֵת צָרָה״.
phrases.english: Blessed are You, ה׳, Who answers in a time of trouble.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next item in the same list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sixth ending recalls יונה in the fish and closes with העונה בעת צרה.

steps.title: The ending of the seventh blessing: He Who answered דוד and שלמה
steps.stepSummary: The last ending recalls דוד and שלמה in ירושלים and closes with 'Who has mercy on the Land.'
steps.simpleTranslation: For the seventh, he says: 'He Who answered דוד and his son שלמה in ירושלים will answer you and hear the sound of your cry on this day. Blessed are You, ה׳, Who has mercy on the Land.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the list with the ending of the seventh ברכה. This is really the sixth added ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When שלמה dedicated the בית המקדש, he prayed that God would send rain when the people pray there (מלכים א ח). So the list ends with 'המרחם על הארץ', a direct request for mercy on the land through rain.

keyTerms.meaning: דוד and his son שלמה, connected to the בית המקדש
Who has mercy on the Land

steps.whatToRemember: Every fast-day ending has the same shape: 'He Who answered [a figure from תנ"ך] will answer you today,' followed by a ברכה that fits the theme. The first is the longer weekday גואל ישראל. Then come זכרונות (ים סוף), שופרות (יהושע), and four more (שמואל, אליהו, יונה, דוד and שלמה).

phrases.english: For the seventh, he says:

phrases.aramaic: ״מִי שֶׁעָנָה אֶת דָּוִד וְאֶת שְׁלֹמֹה בְּנוֹ בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם,
phrases.english: 'He Who answered David and Solomon his son in Jerusalem
He will answer you
and hear the sound of your cry on this day.

phrases.aramaic: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה ה׳ הַמְרַחֵם עַל הָאָרֶץ״.
phrases.english: Blessed are You, ה׳, Who has mercy on the Land.'

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The final ending recalls דוד and שלמה in ירושלים and closes with המרחם על הארץ.

steps.title: Opening of a story
steps.stepSummary: The משנה starts to tell an incident. Only the first word, מעשה, appears on this amud; the story itself continues on the next amud.
steps.whatsHappening: This one word is a setup line. The משנה is about to tell a story, and the story continues in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word מעשה tells us the משנה is switching from listing rules to telling a real event. The event will show how these fast-day practices were actually carried out.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident or story that really happened

phrases.english: An incident (occurred)
phrases.notes: The story continues on the next amud

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the list of endings to a story that illustrates the practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opens a story. Its content continues on the next amud.
